name: Boron deficiency
summary: A controlled Cannabis boron-withholding disorder centered on growing tips, expanding leaves, and root tips. Severe new-growth distortion is useful supporting evidence, but diagnosis should be tied to nutrition and root-zone measurements rather than leaf shape alone.
indicators: Growing tips become stunted before older foliage shows a dominant pattern
New leaflets are distorted, smaller, and narrow near the leaflet base
Advanced new growth curls inward, downward, or at irregular angles and develops marginal necrosis
Severe deficiency can kill growing tips and root tips and lead to whole-plant wilting
exclusions: Distorted tips contain broad mites or hemp russet mites
Root-zone boron supply and tissue analysis are adequate while another exposure explains the distortion
Damage is localized to a spray, heat, or mechanical event
Only old leaves are affected while new growth remains normal

progression.description: Slight stunting develops from the growing tips.
New leaves become narrower and increasingly distorted.
Margins become necrotic, apical tissue can die, root-tip loss can become severe, and the whole plant may wilt.

confirmation: Review fertilizer and source-water boron and measure root-zone pH/EC before assigning the cause.
Use representative tissue analysis when the diagnosis is consequential; the published Cannabis values are experiment-specific, not universal thresholds.
immediateActions: Preserve pre-correction root-zone and tissue measurements.
Inspect distorted growth under magnification for mites before changing nutrition.
correctivePlan: Correct a confirmed boron under-supply gradually with a crop-appropriate nutrition plan.
Track new meristem and root growth; damaged leaves and dead tips will not reverse.
prevention: Maintain complete micronutrient supply and calibrated root-zone monitoring.
Avoid diagnosing micronutrients from internet deficiency charts without measurements.
warnings: The controlled study used one cultivar and complete boron withholding.
Boron has a narrow adequacy-to-toxicity margin in many crops; do not add boron from visual suspicion alone.

sources.title: Characterization of Nutrient Disorders of Cannabis sativa
supportedClaims: Single-element withholding in Cannabis sativa T1 documented boron deficiency, manganese toxicity, and the absence of a visible molybdenum-deficiency phenotype during the nine-week experiment.
Boron-deficient plants developed growing-tip stunting, distorted new leaves, marginal necrosis, death of growing tips, root-tip loss, and severe wilting in advanced stages.

Manganese-toxicity plants developed marginal yellowing of lower leaves progressing inward, marginal necrosis, severe chlorosis, and occasional abscission, but the measured Mn concentration remained within a previously published survey range and biomass did not differ significantly from controls.

Molybdenum-withheld plants had foliar Mo 96% lower than controls yet developed no visual symptoms and no significant dry-weight difference by nine weeks, so a camera-visible Mo-deficiency phenotype was not established.
The experiment used one cultivar and complete withholding or tenfold treatments; tissue values and timing are experimental observations rather than universal Cannabis thresholds.
